limitations.text: Every Cue result comes from a simulator written by the same team that wrote the policy: stalls, pauses, reaction times and interruption costs are assumptions. It shows the policy keeps its caps and trades help against nuisance as designed; it is not evidence about people.

The headline stuck signal is the coach's rule fallback (time since progress). The real hazard model would change when help arrives; an emulated model signal is a secondary sweep and is labelled as an emulation.
Grounding is a fake port right at a chosen rate. Real accuracy on real screens is not measured here; the 60 to 100% sweep is a what-if.

The composite overstates mastery for learners who do not improve and rises 10 points or more in about a third of them. It is experimental and in no headline; independence and the trend are the evidence, and the trend has low power.
A learner who dismisses a cue and then grinds through alone looks independent in the ledger; the guards remove dismiss-and-walk-away and implicit follows within 10 s but cannot remove that leak.
Candidate accuracy is measured on 8 scripted apprentice experts and on experts sampled from the pack's own rules; real experts will do things neither contains.

meta.note: Simulated workers and learners; nothing here is evidence about people. Design targets are design choices.
meta.split: dev population seed 11; held-out seed 77 (separate command)

readings: Candidates: the pack's order rules do most of the work (the same n-gram without them is clearly worse); family A is 8 people with two orderings, so its interval is wide; family B is written from the pack's rules, so it cannot make them lose.

Score: the independence interval and the trend are the headline. The composite overstates for learners who do not improve and rises falsely in about a third of them, so it is shown as experimental only. 'Steady' means cannot tell yet.
Cue: these numbers say how the policy behaves in a simulated world whose assumptions are in PLAN.md and cue/simulate.py. They do not say Cue works on people.

gaming.reading: flat learners whose true skill never changes; a rising score as acceptance falls is gaming inflation
